project_title: PCB Design for ESP32 Project - Power, Main, and Sensor Boards
question: Using the full pre-task conversation, identify the historical requirements and message evidence that are relevant to the current client task. Exclude unrelated history and do not treat the current task itself as historical evidence.

target_task.speaker: client
target_task.text: This arrangement is perfect provided it fits, leaves at least a small gap between the connectors, and does not cover the holes.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Thanks for accepting the invitation, Luka. By 2031-06-15, I’ll send you an initial overview covering 6 boards. We can then discuss the boards, and I’d appreciate your comments, especially about any wrong decisions we should fix.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Sure, that works for me.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Please review this document for the first of 6 boards and let me know whether the design makes sense to you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Would it cause any problems if I waited until next Tuesday to review the PDF?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: That is no problem. Since I just made five changes, I’ll post V6 of the document; please download the latest version next Tuesday before reviewing it.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Thanks; I’ll hold off until you have uploaded the modified document.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: The document review is complete, and we can discuss the project whenever you are free.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: We can use this chat for the discussion. What are your thoughts on the project overall and on this first power PCB?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: For the Power board, it may be worth adding TVS ESD protection.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: For safety, the battery should have protection as well as a fifth NTC terminal.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Thank you for the suggestion; we can add that. Please also propose any further changes you think are needed.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: One point I’m uncertain about is the boost converter: is the plan to disable it through the EN pin to prevent battery drain?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Please make sure the physical length of the I2C connections receives attention.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: By battery protection, are you referring to a hard short circuit across the battery terminals? Overcharge is already handled by the AXP2101, which cuts off at 4.45V, and its overdischarge cutoff is configurable at about ~2.4V. As for NTC, yes, we should add it to J\_BAT.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Yes, I was referring to thermal protection rather than hard-short protection, because the component supports that too.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: All the suggestions so far look good, thank you. I still need to update the document with them.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: For the boost converter, connect EN to GPIO3 rather than tying it HIGH, so I can switch it off and on programmatically.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: That boost-control change will be added to the document.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Will deep-sleep mode be used by the ESP32?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: With I2C interboard cables limited to ≤30cm, the setup should work at 800kHz using the existing 4.4kΩ pull-ups.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: At present, the ESP32 runs at 240MHz max and drops to 120MHz while idle through automatic light sleep. It enters deep sleep at about ~35µA only when the battery is critical or after a false wake. The wake sources are a 20min timer and the touch button on GPIO 26 ext0. In the final version, however, I will keep it in deep sleep most of the time and wake it only for updates. Does that mean some pins need to move, perhaps AXP IRQ?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Should we also reconsider the boost EN pin?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: In that case, adding a pull-down resistor to the boost converter’s EN pin might be better.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: All your suggested updates are being incorporated into the v8 I’m preparing, and I’ll take the pull-down proposal into account as well. Thanks.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: A 330kΩ pull-down has now been placed on MT3608 EN.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Until the ESP32 enables it, the boost converter will therefore remain off.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Yes—the boost converter supplies the sensors that require 5V.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Those sensors will operate only periodically rather than running continuously.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Yes, operating them periodically will lower battery consumption.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Please review V8 and let me know if you have any further suggestions; everything you have proposed so far has been very helpful.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I'll check the updated document.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Should I begin the Hire process? I’m ready to do so on 2031-06-15.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Apologies, it's been a long day.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: What completion date do you need for this part of the project?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Although there is no hard deadline, completing it sooner would of course be preferable, as always.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Could you give me at least an approximate completion target?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Since I really don't know how much time this normally requires, I was hoping for delivery within a few days. Please tell me if that expectation is unrealistic.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: To plan around my other projects, I need to know whether I can finish on time; a couple of days is workable.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: If a couple of days is the turnaround for each board, that works for me.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Ok

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I’ll proceed with the hire by clicking the button right away.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Thanks; I’m glad to take on the project.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: You're welcome. I confirmed your offer exactly as submitted and completed the hire.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Before you begin, here is V7. The I2C pull-ups were removed from this board because they have been moved to the main board, and that is the revision’s only change.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Anything you think could be useful, please post here.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Since the HRO TYPE-C-31-M-17 is 6p and has no D+ or D- data lines, the USB connector must be replaced.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: A standard, readily sourced connector is fine; just make sure it is easy to obtain. If it is available on AliExpress, that is a sufficient check.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Would the following part work as the replacement?
<https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C2760486.html?s_z=n_HRO%2520TYPE-C-31-M-%252017>

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Availability is my only concern. This premium option normally costs 1.46$, while typical ones are 0.4$; we can use it provided compatible alternatives exist if it goes out of stock, since I do not want a part that may be unavailable regularly.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Can you provide the PCB shape and connector locations, and confirm whether PCB mounting holes are required?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Inside the case, the board will lie horizontally, with the USB protruding slightly from the shorter edge. For mounting, 8 holes at the corners will be enough.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Dimensions, shape?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Keep the board as small as the components permit, with USB-C on the shorter edge and 8 mounting holes sized M2.5 at the corners. A roughly 4:2 aspect ratio is preferred; it should not be square.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: To let you review the design and identify any changes, I'll send the files within 3 days. I also need to know which kind of LED should provide the battery-charge indication.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Battery-charge status should be shown by the SK6812 addressable LED chain on GPIO13, which is on the main board. No separate LED is needed; thank you for clarifying the LED requirement.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: From what I can see so far, it looks great, and I think that is everything. Thanks; once I receive the files, I can inspect them more closely.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: For the design, which connectors would you like me to use?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Which arrangement should I follow—the first picture or the second one?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Use the vertical JST arrangement shown in the first picture. I have one concern because this assembly will plug into a base, so I'll send an image now to explain it more easily.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Ok

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Plugging it in with this orientation would prevent me from connecting the battery underneath.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Because the support is currently 3d printed and there are now 8 holes, I could make a different support that uses screws to secure it. However, it still has to fit vertically in this orientation.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Vertically, like those green PCBs?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Ideally, the battery JST would sit next to the board JST, with both vertical, as shown in AM\_1.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I believe I understand it.
